messages:
maria: Heads-up — planning next quarter GPU commits. Getting conflicting p95/p99 SLO math for chat workloads. Quick thread to align on assumptions and admission control thresholds. Current baseline: avg request tokens 60, model = redwood-vicuna-13b, avg generation latency per request ≈ 220ms on p4d with batch tuning. QPS observed 120 during peak. Need to compute GPU hours for 3x seasonal peak margin. Thoughts?

 dan: Couple of quick checks — where'd the 220ms come from? Is that network-inclusive or pure inference? Also are we treating batching as continuous batching or per-request? :thinking: 

 maria: 220ms is end-to-end from request enter runtime to first token+generation finish — includes small network hop inside infra but not client network. Continuous batching enabled with 64ms micro-batch window. Effective batch size avg 8. Service time per request (s) =~ 0.22s/req.

 leo: For SLOs, use queueing model. If we approximate M/M/c it's messy; easier to compute utilization ρ = λ * s / c. For p95/p99, we keep ρ well below 1. For p99 < 1s target, rule of thumb ρ ≤ 0.6 for chat gen where variability high. That gives headroom for batching spikes.

 ashley: Agree. If peak λ = 120 qps, s=0.22s, required c such that ρ = λ*s/c ≤0.6 -> c ≥ λ*s/0.6 = 120*0.22/0.6 ≈ 44 GPUs. That's a lot. Are we using sharded multi-GPU per inference? We typically place a single model replica per GPU for that model, so c = number of model replicas.

 dan: Quick calc notes: GPU throughput per replica = 1/s ≈ 4.55 req/s. So 44 GPUs ~ 200 req/s capacity at 0.6 utilization. Matches above.

 ashley: For GPU hours: assume we run that pool 24/7 for quarter (90d). Hours = 44 * 24 * 90 = 95040 GPU-hours. For 3x seasonal peak margin we might plan for 44*3 = 132 GPUs -> 285120 GPU-hours. Put that against committed vs burstable capacity.

 leo: For admission control and p99, we can implement token-bucket shaped admission where we accept requests up to ρ_target per replica. Practical rule: throttle when in-flight requests per replica >= inflight_threshold = floor(1/ s * ρ_target * safety_factor). Example: ρ_target=0.6, safety_factor=0.9 -> inflight_threshold ≈ floor(4.55*0.6*0.9)=2. So only 2 concurrent requests allowed per replica. If the runtime queues beyond that, shed or route to cheaper model.

 maria: Nice. Any equation snippet we can add to the runbook for on-call? e.g., ρ = λ*s/c; GPUs_needed = ceil(λ*s/ρ_target). Also GPU_hours = GPUs_needed * 24 * days.

 ashley: Add p99 latency bound approx using Kingman's formula for G/G/1 wait: E[W_q] ≈ (ρ/(1-ρ)) * (c_a^2 + c_s^2)/2 * s. We can put conservative c_a^2 + c_s^2 = 2.5 for chat. If we want E[sojourn] = s + E[W_q] <= p99_target. These are approximations but useful.

 dan: Implementation notes: metric names to monitor: infra.request_rate(model), infra.inflight_per_replica, infra.replica_utilization, infra.queue_latency_p99. Need alert when utilization >0.55 and queue_latency_p95 > 200ms.

 maria: OK I'll update capacity plan and runbook with these numbers and thresholds. Action items: @ashley to produce cost estimate for 132 GPUs across quarter, @leo to draft admission-control logic + runtime patch, @dan to add alerts. ETA EOD tomorrow.

 infra-bot: deploy status: canary admission-control patch in staging at 2024-04-02T21:10Z

 ashley: noted. I'll send estimated committed vs on-demand cost breakdown by EOD.

 maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
